title: Events, the log as a data structure, and why order matters

videos.script: A customer buys two copies of a book in Olinda. {{sale}} You can write that down in two ways. You can change a number: Olinda now has three copies. Or you can write down what happened: two copies sold, at this till, at this minute. {{two-ways}} The number tells you where things stand. The record tells you how they got there, and from the records you can always work out the number again. {{fold}} This lesson is about the second way. A list of things that happened, kept in order, that nobody edits. That list is called a log, and it is what Kafka stores. {{log}} You will write one in twenty-five lines of Python. Then you will compute the stock of a book from it, shuffle the same events, and watch the stock come out wrong. {{shuffle}} Order matters. But not all of it. Only the order of events about the same thing, and that is what makes a log possible to spread over many machines. {{per-key}}
